fact: The CEMAC QR Code standard, launched 29 July 2026 across six states including Equatorial Guinea, lets a client with a bank account, mobile money wallet or microfinance account pay by scan whatever their institution.
GIMACPAY, the CEMAC card-mobile-transfer ecosystem in service since 2021, processed over sixteen million mobile transactions in 2025.
GIMACPAY links 56 banks, 26 microfinance institutions, 16 payment institutions and mobile money operators and 52 aggregators across the CEMAC, which processed 20.3 million transactions in 2025.
The Fintech Times says mobile money, for example Orange Money operating across Central Africa, is the primary entry point to digital finance in Equatorial Guinea.
The World Bank diagnostic says digital financial services are nascent, with no licensed e-money operator for mobile money.

fact: AfricaNenda says GIMACPAY, live since July 2020, carries P2P and merchant payments to and from 11 mobile money operators across the six CEMAC states including Equatorial Guinea.
AfricaNenda says GIMACPAY gives all-to-all interoperability between banks, microfinance institutions and mobile money operators in the six CEMAC states including Equatorial Guinea.
AfricaNenda says GIMACPAY also provides domestic instant payment functionality connecting banks and mobile money wallets in each CEMAC state, including Equatorial Guinea.
